html:
English playwright and poet, born in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1564. His plays are performed and quoted more than any others in the world.

He moved to London and wrote for the stage under Elizabeth I and then James I. He was an actor and part owner of his company, which played at the Globe Theatre on the south bank of the Thames.

His work, about 39 plays plus poems, falls into rough groups:

  • Histories of English kings, such as Richard III and Henry V.
  • Comedies, such as A Midsummer Night's Dream and Twelfth Night.
  • Tragedies, such as Hamlet, Othello, King Lear and Macbeth.
  • Late romances, such as The Tempest, and 154 sonnets.

He shaped the English language, and many common phrases first appear in his lines. He retired to Stratford and died there in 1616, the same year as Cervantes. Friends gathered his plays into the First Folio of 1623; without it about half of them would be lost.
sum: English playwright and poet, born in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1564. His plays are performed and quoted more than any others in the world.
